newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan dollar ends down as exports' move slows.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan dollar ends down as exports' move slows.

text.p: The Taiwan dollar reversed early gains to close slightly lower against its American counterpart on Monday as exports' U.S. dollar sales slowed, dealers said.
Despite moving as high as T$27.425, the local dollar ended at T$27.442 against Saturday's T$27.435 close.
Turnover through dealers was an active US$320 million.
Dealers noted saw some foreign fund inflows, but said they were not heavy enough to trigger a Taiwan dollar rise.
The local dollar has been strong recently despite the U.S. dollar's steady rise overseas due to funding needs by exporters before the Chinese new year holiday starting on February 6.

That local demand appeared to be slowing, they said, with some saying Monday may have been the final day of pre-holiday Taiwan dollar buying by many local enterprises, even though the foreign exchange market will trade on Tuesday and Wednesday.
"Such Taiwan dollar needs have slowed today and many investors expect the Taiwan dollar to depreciate after the Chinese new year," said one dealer.

Analysts said the seasonal Taiwan dollar demand had let the local dollar defy a general depreciation seen in many other Asian regional currencies, but that this was likely to end once the seasonal demand expires, with a depreciation likely.
"The Taiwan dollar may fall to test T$27.50 after the new year holiday," the dealer said.
For Tuesday, a T$27.44-27.47 range was seen.
